sense.text:
“Make bright the arrows; gather the shields” means prepare for war. “The Lord hath raised up the spirit of the kings of the Medes”: the kings of the Medes is Iran.

“For his device is against Babylon, to destroy it; because it is the vengeance of the Lord, the vengeance of his temple.” That is God’s judgment. He is going to pay Babylon back for what was done to Israel, God’s people, and for the temple itself.

This is being fulfilled before our eyes. The US and Israel launched their strikes on Iran, and Iran answered with rockets on Dubai, on Qatar, and on the US Fifth Fleet headquarters in Manama. Iran may not yet have long-range missiles that reach America, but it is hitting all the neighbours that are friendly with America. Things are happening all around us while we play in our sins.

“Set up the standard upon the walls of Babylon, make the watch strong”: God is telling America, make your watch strong. Set up your watchmen, prepare your ambushes, your liers in wait.

“For the Lord hath both devised and done that which he spake against the inhabitants of Babylon.” What he said in his scriptures he is going to do to Babylon, he is going to make sure it is carried out.

“O thou that dwellest upon many waters” is America. America dwells upon many waters: look at the map around Saudi Arabia and the Horn of Africa and America has military bases all over it. Those bases are what Iran is trying to hit.

“Abundant in treasures” means America is rich, filthy rich. “Thine end is come, and the measure of thy covetousness”: because they covet lands and take them by violence.

What do caterpillars do to a tree? They eat it from within. Caterpillars destroy trees from within. “Surely I will fill thee with men, as with caterpillers”: those men are the terrorists, the sleeper cells. “And they shall lift up a shout against thee”: that is the Allahu Akbar that they scream.

The map of Iran’s retaliation shows the long-term US military bases it hit, all of them in US-friendly places. And now they say Khamenei is dead. But the Ayatollah Khamenei is revered and loved throughout the whole Muslim world, Shiites and Sunnis, and he has people that love and adore him in this country, real Muslims. If you think it is just going to end with his death, it is not.

While war is taking place, and this is one of the birth pains, God is saying to us, “My people, go ye out of the midst of her.” “And deliver ye every man his soul from the fierce anger of the Lord”: deliver your soul from this place. If your soul is entangled here in Babylon the Great, you will get caught up in the fierce anger of the Lord.

“And lest your heart faint, and ye fear for the rumour that shall be heard in the land.” A rumour is something spoken about that has not yet occurred. Iran going to war with America and Israel was a rumour, and now we see it is a reality. How long is it going to last? It could last a few days and pause: a birth pain.

“A rumour shall both come one year, and after that in another year shall come a rumour, and violence in the land, ruler against ruler.”

Habakkuk was complaining about the nations, Babylon and the other nations ruling over us. “I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower, and will watch to see what he will say unto me.” This chapter is where the caterpillars of Jeremiah 51 come in, and we have been prophesying this thing a long time.

“Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables”: God wants this vision plain in the book, this book, the Bible. “That he may run that readeth it”: they are reading it, but they don’t understand. They are running, trying to find out what it is talking about.
“For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry.”

“Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him.” The soul in the white man is not upright in him. He is not a just man. He might smile in your face, he might do a nice thing for you occasionally, but his soul is not right. God created him, and God knows what he is talking about.

“But the just shall live by his faith”: the faith we have to live by is Christ.

“Yea also, because he transgresseth by wine”: the wine he transgresses by is his Christianity and his democracy, which are virtually the same thing. Christianity is just the other side of democracy. It is his policies, his religions, his politics.

“He is a proud man”: Edom. “Neither keepeth at home”: he does not mind his business. He is in everybody’s business. America is a busybody, telling the people of Iran to revolt, overthrow, this is your opportunity to change the regime.

“Who enlargeth his desire as hell”: every place he goes he steals, he takes, and it becomes a hell on earth. “And is as death”: this man, his religions and his politics are as death. “And cannot be satisfied”: he could not be satisfied with just stealing America; he has to enlarge his empire.

“But gathereth unto him all nations, and heapeth unto him all people.” He goes to country after country implementing his policies and his religion, and causes hell and death in those lands through bombs and war, whether economic war or firepower. Then the residue of the people of the countries he destabilized, he lets them come to America, to Europe, to England. That is how he gathers unto him all nations.

“Shall not all these”: these people that he heaped unto him, in his own country, “take up a parable against him, and a taunting proverb against him.” This goes with the caterpillars of Jeremiah 51 that lift up a shout against him.

“Woe” means destruction: destruction “to him that increaseth that which is not his!” Iran does not belong to him, but he is trying to implement his policies in Iran. He hit Syria, Somalia, Yemen, Afghanistan. Those are not his countries, but he hits them economically and with conventional weapons, then he puts his policies in place.

“How long?” How long shall this man be in everybody’s country with war, economic or conventional? “And to him that ladeth himself with thick clay”: the thick clay goes back to the bottom of verse 5, “heapeth unto him all people”, and goes with the last kingdom of Daniel 2, part iron and part clay.

“Shall they not rise up suddenly that shall bite thee”: these are the caterpillars Jeremiah told us about. Rise up from what? Sleep. “Suddenly” is terrorism. “And awake that shall vex thee”: they shall vex this place. “And thou shalt be for booties unto them”: they will take America down from within. It is going to start like that, slowly but surely.

If you want to know why terrorism is going to happen, it says right here: “Because thou hast spoiled many nations, all the remnant of the people shall spoil thee.” America, you spoiled many nations, and the remnant of the people within your country shall spoil you.

“Because of men’s blood.” When America drops bombs on places, it kills civilians, innocent women and children. And war is economic too. When they forbid Venezuela to sell oil to Cuba, no oil goes to Cuba: no gas, the cars don’t run, sanitation doesn’t run, no electricity, the hospitals don’t work, and the people in those hospitals are dead. You don’t think their family members are angry?

“And for the violence of the land, of the city, and of all that dwell therein.” These are the things that are happening. All we can do is wait for the I-told-you-so moment, because we have been prophesying this thing for a long time.

precepts.why:
“Now go, write it before them in a table, and note it in a book, that it may be for the time to come for ever and ever.” The table is the book, the book of the Lord.

So when the Lord tells Habakkuk to “make it plain upon tables”, he is saying, I want this vision plain in the book, the Bible, for the time to come.

“Behold, the days come, saith the Lord God, that I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the Lord.”

“They shall run to and fro to seek the word of the Lord, and shall not find it.” Why? Because they are going to the Catholics, they are going to the Baptists, looking for the word. They are not running to the Israelites; they are running to every other religion, asking what the Bible says about what is going on, and they are not going to understand it. They are not going to hear the word of the Lord.

That is the running of Habakkuk 2:2: “that he may run that readeth it.” They read it, but they don’t understand, and they run trying to find out what it is talking about.

“If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink; he shall even be the prophet of this people.”

By this verse, wine represents the spirit and falsehood, walking in the spirit and falsehood and lies. So the wine the proud man “transgresseth by” in Habakkuk 2:5 is his Christianity and his democracy: his religions, his policies, his politics.

“The vision of Obadiah. Thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom; We have heard a rumour from the Lord, and an ambassador is sent among the heathen”: someone is going to rise up among the nations and say, “Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in battle.” Let us go against America, against Israel, in battle.

“The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee”: that is what we wanted to get to. Edom is the proud man of Habakkuk 2:5.

“Thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock”: they came from the Caucasus Mountains and dwelt in the clefts of the rock in the Middle Ages. In Obadiah’s time it was the place called Petra today; look at the architecture, just like Rome, just like Washington D.C. “Whose habitation is high”: their skyscrapers. “That saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” To make that statement you have to have power. They are saying nobody can beat us.

“Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle”: not only is Edom a proud people, their symbol is the eagle. Take out your dollar bill: the animal symbol of America is the eagle. “And though thou set thy nest among the stars”: who is sending satellites, who is doing space travel? America.

People say Edom is the Arabs. Edom is not the Arabs: the Arabs are not doing space travel, and their symbol is not the eagle. Others say it is the American Indian, because they use the eagle. It is not them either: if they had power, they would have blown the white man off the face of the earth. People throw these things out to confuse the new converts.

“Thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.”

sense.text:
Our people are now saying, we don’t want to vote Democratic anymore, we want to be Republicans. They really think the Republican Party is the party for black people. But God said deliver your soul from this place: come out of her religions, come out of her politics, because for many of them their politics is their religion.

“As for us, our eyes as yet failed for our vain help: in our watching we have watched for a nation that could not save us.” We jump from one political party to the next, saying America can surely save us with this party. It is a nation that cannot save us.

Notice what the Bible prophesies: “They hunt our steps, that we cannot go in our streets.” “Our end is near, our days are fulfilled; for our end is come.”

The Epstein emails show Epstein going to a party to hunt, and the hunt was black people, called by the N-word. Maria Farmer said that group was incredibly elitist and incredibly racist. The movie Surviving the Game, where Ice-T is taken into the wilderness by a group of men to be the one hunted, we watched as entertainment; now with Epstein we find out it was true. There is always some truth behind these movies. Epstein was hunting black people, him and his friends. Remember Oprah Winfrey had black students in South Africa that disappeared, and they don’t know where a lot of those girls went; then they found out Oprah was very good friends with Epstein.

In case you don’t know this is talking about America: “Our persecutors are swifter than the eagles of the heaven.” What is the symbol of America? The eagle.

“They pursued us upon the mountains, they laid wait for us in the wilderness.” Peter Spencer, a Jamaican immigrant, was invited on a hunting trip with a group of white men in Pennsylvania and was shot nine times, and the man who shot him was not charged. They took him on a hunting trip and he was the prey. Rasheem Carter was hunted through the woods, running for his life, and when he was found his skull was cut in half, and they said an animal did it. Animals can’t do that. These are your friendly neighbourhood white people.

“I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions”: God has multiplied visions. “And used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.” A similitude is one thing likened to another.

So we will read about a country that did exist, but God is not really talking about that country you are reading about. Ezekiel 28 and the prince of Tyrus is the example: a similitude for today.

“Say unto the prince of Tyrus”: the prince of Tyrus is a metaphor for today, for America, for the white man, Esau Edom.

“Because thine heart is lifted up, and thou hast said, I am a God, I sit in the seat of God, in the midst of the seas.” America is the only one in the midst of the seas, everywhere on the planet. It is not China, it is not the Arabs, and it is not Africa for sure.

They are the only ones that set themselves up as God. Look at the image of God they always paint: the bust of the Saviour, Salvator, with the crown of thorns, found in the Church of San Salvatore in Termis, for which it is an open secret that Cesare Borgia, the son of Pope Alexander, posed; and the sketches Leonardo did of Cesare Borgia as the new Renaissance Jesus. All this time you have been praying to this white man, and it is Cesare Borgia: a pedophile, a pervert, a murderer, who had sex with his sister Lucrezia. A nasty Edomite. So connect the dots: who sets himself up as God, claiming he has God, and is everywhere? This so-called white man, mainly America.

“Yet thou art a man, and not God, though thou set thine heart as the heart of God.” It is not God; it says you are a man. You really believe you are God.

“Behold, thou art wiser than Daniel; there is no secret that they can hide from thee.” Daniel was the wisest prophet, able to interpret dreams and understand them, and the Bible prophesies that this man is wiser than Daniel; you cannot hide secrets from him.

How? His technology. We think he made it because he loves us, but no: it is to survey us, to monitor us. That is what your iPhones, your Androids and your smart TVs are, to see what we are doing, how we are doing it, and how often.

“With thy wisdom and with thine understanding thou hast gotten thee riches”: that is their tax revenue system; that is how they got wealthy.

“And hast gotten gold and silver into thy treasures”: the IMF and the World Bank, their two major financial institutions, right across the street from one another in Washington D.C. They make the international economic plans with countries and give out foreign aid, and if you can’t pay it back, and you can’t, you owe the big bad wolf. Kwame Nkrumah called it neo-colonialism, a financial trap you can never get out of. That is why they got mad at Captain Ibrahim Traore: he got his gold, paid his debts back, and said, get out of my country. But he is one of the few.

“By thy great wisdom and by thy traffick hast thou increased thy riches”: traffick means trade.

“And thine heart is lifted up because of thy riches.” Don’t let America fool you saying, we’re in debt, we’re broke, we’re poor. America prints its own money; its debt is in its own money. How can you owe yourself? Print it, and it is paid. That is all they do.

“Because thou hast set thine heart as the heart of God; Behold, therefore I will bring strangers upon thee, the terrible of the nations”: the terrible of the nations means the terrorists of the nations, terrorist nations. “And they shall draw their swords against the beauty of thy wisdom, and they shall defile thy brightness.”

“They shall bring thee down to the pit, and thou shalt die the deaths of them that are slain in the midst of the seas.” In the midst of the seas their military is going to be wiped out. This is going to take time.

precepts.why:
Ezekiel used the similitude of the prince of Tyrus; Isaiah 14 is talking about the same thing. “Thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon, and say, How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!” Babylon is an oppressing city, and it is wealthy.

“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning!” God is calling Babylon Lucifer, meaning light bearer. “How art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!” Babylon weakens the nations economically and conventionally, with war.

“They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms.” He is not a god. It says, “Is this the man”: the man that made the earth to tremble with war.

That is the same as Ezekiel 28: “yet thou art a man, and not God.”

“And that no man might buy or sell, save he that had the mark, or the name of the beast, or the number of his name.” This beast we always read about: “count the number of the beast: for it is the number of a man.” A man.

The Bible is written like a puzzle, so put the pieces together. In Ezekiel 28 this man set himself up and said he is God and sits in the seat of God, but he is a man. Isaiah 14 called Babylon Lucifer, but it was a man. In Revelation 13 the beast is a man, and his number is 666. It is all going into the same man.

sense.text:
This whole chapter deals with Esau’s rulership: from the white horse to the red horse, and now the black horse. The black horse represents the dark nations that Esau is over.

“I heard the third beast say, Come and see”: this third beast, a powerful angel, says to John, I’m going to show you something. “And lo a black horse; and he that sat on him had a pair of balances in his hand.” This white man sitting on the black horse holds the balances, a scale of right and wrong weight and measure.

“A measure of wheat for a penny, and three measures of barley for a penny.” Who dictates how much wheat costs worldwide? America, with its World Bank and its IMF. They control the economy of the world. They are the ones that say Jamaica’s money is no good, Sierra Leone’s money is no good, Haiti’s money is garbage. Yet those countries have the resources and America does not. But might makes right: America has the military arsenal, so all nations have to keep quiet.

“And see thou hurt not the oil and the wine”: “see thou” means do not deal unjustly. Verses 5 and 6 are speaking of the IMF and the World Bank, the world economy.

And our people try to get into this world, into America’s wealth and riches. They want a piece of the pie, and getting a piece of America’s pie is dangerous.

precepts.why:
Christ asks the question: “For what is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?”

To get the fame and fortune that so many of our people desperately want, because we want to take care of our friends and family, you have to sell your soul. You must give your soul to these people. That is the price of a piece of the pie the man on the black horse holds.

sense.text:
“And the merchants of the earth shall weep and mourn over her”: the merchants of the earth are the corporations, and this includes the IMF and the World Bank. They make major deals with countries.

Our people want to get involved in this world economy, and what they get is often hush money. LeBron James takes care of his friends and family, which is admirable, but he is not allowed to help his people on a major level. Hush money: just take care of your friends and family. Oprah and so many of these black celebrities, many of them went to Epstein’s island, and their names are on the list.

See how it works with the Chinese restaurants in black neighbourhoods. The Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882 banned Chinese labourers but left a loophole for merchants, and in 1915 a court ruled that owning a restaurant counted as a business. Then in the 1960s the banks would not lend for Chinese restaurants in white neighbourhoods, but gave Asian Americans loans to open businesses in black communities while black people could not get loans to open businesses in their own communities. They are given grants to learn how the local community talks; they don’t need good credit. Credit is just for us.

And look at the debt. America is never going to pay its debt; its debt is in its own currency, and it can simply print it. Africa’s debt is in US dollars. The World Bank’s principle is that no country should grow its own food: Africa and the third world grow export crops and buy their grain from the United States or Europe, so that when they do something America doesn’t like, America can sanction them and starve them. They take a billion dollars’ worth of gold and give you five cents for it. That is what America did to Iran: years of sanctions crushed its economy, and now he says to the people, overthrow your government, with a puppet leader already waiting.

“The merchandise of gold, and silver, and precious stones, and of pearls”: it comes by the ships, in those big containers on the seas. The majority of what we are reading here comes from the continent of Africa.
“And slaves”: that was you and me. “And souls of men.” You want a piece of the pie, you have to sell your soul. There are things you must do.

precepts.why:
“Why is earth and ashes proud?” Earth and ashes represents man: why is man proud? “There is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man.” They covet what does not belong to them, what is not theirs. If you are covetous, you want a piece of the American pie, you want those billions of dollars in contracts.

“For such an one setteth his own soul to sale; because while he liveth he casteth away his bowels.” While he lives he casts away his bowels: the lower intestine, the rectum. You cast it away. Take it.

You think Oprah got all that money just because she was a great talk show host? You think LeBron and these athletes got those contracts because nobody is as good as them? Actors like Michael Jai White don’t get the contracts the other Hollywood stars get. It is not that he can’t act; he is a good actor. There are certain things he said he is not going to do, so he does not get a piece of the American pie. That is the soul of men sold in the merchandise of Babylon.

“But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare.” Everybody says, I want to be rich; people come to this country to be rich. Tyler Perry’s movie Temptation shows it: a woman with a good marriage is tempted by a rich, famous man with his own jet; she is covetous, he entices her into the rich life and drugs, she catches HIV, and her whole life is ruined.

“And into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.” That is why Ye said, if you see a video of me doing something with a goat: he knew what he did to get where he is, and he knew they were dangling it over his head. We’ll embarrass you; we got you on tape. They have something on all of those Hollywood actors. Our people can repent, but they fear that if they repent and give their lives to the Lord they will be publicly humiliated for the things they did to get their fortunes. Look at what they did to Wendy Williams: in 2020 she said she would not take the vaccine, Dr. Oz told her millions of people follow her, and after that they destroyed her. She cannot even take care of her own money.

“For the love of money is the root of all evil”: not money itself, but the love of it. “Which while some coveted after” is the key. Covetousness is the last of the ten commandments, and it starts in your mind. If you will covet, you will break the eighth commandment and steal; if you steal you will lie, the ninth; and you will murder, the sixth. It is a domino effect through God’s commandments. Covetousness is the root of all sins.

“They have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.” A young lady from our Houston school wanted to be America’s Next Top Model; she said her friends told her the white man was a devil and she didn’t believe it, and they put her through the wringer: to get that modeling contract she had to cast her bowels. In the movie Black Starlet a woman is told to sleep with the producer to star in the film; when she has done it she is told, my dear, there are many producers, and there is a line of them at the door. Sukihana cried that she signed a contract, sold her soul to the devil, and did not know if God could hear her; then she got the phone call and went right back into the music business.

“But thou, O man of God, flee these things”: flee coveting after money. There is nothing wrong with getting a better job or a higher education to make money, but when you covet money you are going about it in a spiritually disastrous way. “And follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness. Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life.”

“For all nations have drunk of the wine of the wrath of her fornication.” This wine is the same wine we read about in Habakkuk 2:5: her policies.

“And the kings of the earth have committed fornication with her”: the kings of the earth are called presidents and prime ministers today, and they do business with Babylon the Great. “And the merchants of the earth are waxed rich through the abundance of her delicacies”: the merchants are the corporations.

sense.text: That is what Paul was saying to Timothy in the first letter, and he continues in the second. “Stir up the gift of God, which is in thee by the putting on of my hands”: Timothy, you have the Holy Spirit on you; stir that gift up, don’t let it lie. Not to stir it up is to bury your talent in the ground, to put it in a napkin like the parables Christ gave, and do nothing with it.

“For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” Paul is telling Timothy, you have nothing to be afraid of. Do the work. Stir up the gift of the Holy Spirit within you. Why does he mention fear? Because of the afflictions that were going on.

“Be not thou therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner”: don’t be ashamed of Christ, and don’t be ashamed of me. “But be thou partaker of the afflictions of the gospel according to the power of God.” Afflictions were on the rise for the believers, and that is why Paul was telling Timothy not to be afraid.

“Who hath saved us, and called us with an holy calling, not according to our works.” We all have that holy calling, and we are not called into this truth because of some good works we did, something so magnanimous that God said, I’ll choose this person. “But according to his own purpose and grace”: God saw something in you that you didn’t know was there. I’ll call that brother and that sister; I see greatness in them.

“Which was given us in Christ Jesus before the world began.” We were with the Lord in the beginning, all of us, and we were given a gift. What Paul says to Timothy he is saying to us. We used to say, I ain’t nobody, I ain’t got nothing in me. No: you have more than you think. We were given understanding, a gift, before the world began.

“But is now made manifest by the appearing of our Saviour Jesus Christ, who hath abolished death.” When Christ rose from the dead, he abolished death: by believing in me, I abolished death; I’m the King, I’m the Lord; come unto me.

“And hath brought life and immortality to light through the gospel”: life and immortality come to light only through the gospel, the good news.
“Whereunto I am appointed a preacher”: preacher means prophet. “And an apostle, and a teacher of the Gentiles.” Paul had a multitude of gifts.

“For the which cause I also suffer these things”: because he is appointed a preacher, an apostle and a teacher, he suffers the afflictions. “Nevertheless I am not ashamed”: I might be in and out of jail for preaching this gospel, but I’m not ashamed and I’m not going to stop.

“For I know whom I have believed, and am persuaded that he is able to keep that which I have committed unto him against that day.” Paul committed his soul, his life, to Christ. And that day is the second coming.

“Hold fast the form of sound words”: the doctrine we are teaching, the gospel, is sound words. Hold fast to that; don’t let it go. If we hold fast to these sound words, it will enrich us personally, in our marriages, in our families, as a community and as a nation.
“That good thing which was committed unto thee keep by the Holy Ghost which dwelleth in us.” That is why he said, stir up the gift that is within you.

“All they which are in Asia be turned away from me; of whom are Phygellus and Hermogenes.” Men that stood strong in this gospel, men that warred with Paul, left. They left the faith.

This is what we have warned you brothers and sisters about. We have seen a lot come and a lot go, so don’t get too attached. You’re strong today, but we’ll see about tomorrow, when affliction, tribulation and persecution come. That is why Paul told Timothy, stir up the gift, and God has not given us the spirit of fear: because of the afflictions.

“The Lord give mercy unto the house of Onesiphorus; for he oft refreshed me, and was not ashamed of my chain.” Paul prays God bless this brother: he was not ashamed that Paul was locked up in prison. Paul was telling Timothy not to be ashamed of the gospel because he saw that spirit coming on Timothy.

“But, when he was in Rome, he sought me out very diligently, and found me.” There were no cell phones then; he had to go on foot and find Paul.

“The Lord grant unto him that he may find mercy of the Lord in that day”: that same day we have been reading about, the day of the Lord. “And in how many things he ministered unto me at Ephesus, thou knowest very well”: this brother even helped Paul in Ephesus, and Timothy knew it.

precepts.why:
Paul said the same thing to the brothers at Ephesus: “According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world.”

That is what he reminded Timothy of: grace “given us in Christ Jesus before the world began.” All you believers were there before the foundation of the world. Before let there be light, you were there. The earth was made on the third day, and we were before that.

“The Lord shall preserve thee from all evil: he shall preserve thy soul.”

That is what Sukihana and all our people in the entertainment world and the sports world need to see. You might think you have sold your soul to the devil, but God preserves your soul. Paul was persuaded that the Lord “is able to keep that which I have committed unto him.” So don’t let your circumstances drive you into a world of sin, evil and debauchery. Come out of that lifestyle.

This explains the day Paul is talking about. “Now we beseech you, brethren, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by our gathering together unto him”: all twelve tribes can only gather unto Christ.

“That ye be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as from us, as that the day of Christ is at hand.” People were writing letters in Paul’s name saying the day of Christ had already come and gone. Paul said, I don’t care if you got a letter signed by me; I didn’t write it, and that day has not happened yet. In the 1960s the FBI did the same thing, writing letters to the Black Panthers and other black organizations in each other’s names.

“Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first.” Christians say that means people leaving Christianity. It is not talking about that. Christ is not going to return until all twelve tribes fall away into captivity. In Paul’s time Judah, Benjamin and Levi had not yet fallen completely; they were still in the land, and 70 AD was soon approaching.

What is the falling away? “And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations”: they shall fall, meaning all twelve tribes shall fall.

“And Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.” We are still living in the times of the Gentiles, and what has happened to us? We all fell into captivity. That falling away has to come before that day.

That day Paul spoke of to Timothy, “against that day”, is the second coming. “The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood”: this is a time of war and devastation, “before the great and the terrible day of the Lord come.” When Christ returns, it is going to be a great and terrible day.

“Woe unto you that desire the day of the Lord!” We say, I can’t wait for the day of the Lord, because we don’t really comprehend the magnitude of what is going to happen on that day. “To what end is it for you? the day of the Lord is darkness, and not light.”

You think it is going to be a bright day, with Christ taking us all up to the kingdom. It is not that type of day; it is not that type of party.

“The great day of the Lord is near, it is near, and hasteth greatly, even the voice of the day of the Lord: the mighty man shall cry there bitterly. That day is a day of wrath, a day of trouble and distress.”

So don’t think that when the Lord returns we are all going to be standing and cheering. No: we are going to be running and weeping.

“Immediately after the tribulation of those days”: tribulation will come, and that is Jacob’s trouble. “Shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light”: because the sky will be black. “And the stars shall fall from heaven”: missiles dropping from the sky. “And the powers of the heavens shall be shaken”: the powers of the nations shaken with war.

“And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn.” You think you are going to be happy, stomping your feet and clapping? That is not what the Bible says. All the tribes of the earth shall mourn, meaning cry bitterly, “and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.”

“But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance”: your history, back to your remembrance.

“Whatsoever I have said unto you.” Christ said a lot: if you love me, keep my commandments; you shall fall by the edge of the sword and be led away captive into all nations until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled. He was telling us, you are going into slavery, Israel, but don’t worry, I am sending the Holy Ghost to you.

Why does the Holy Ghost have to bring all things to our remembrance? Because we would lose our identity, our history. We thought we were Afro-American; some of you thought you were Puerto Rican, some thought you were Dominican. Every last one of us lost our way. Our knowing who we are is the evidence that the Holy Ghost is back. That is the good thing committed unto us, kept by the Holy Ghost which dwells in us.

“For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica.” Demas travelled with Paul and warred with Paul, and he forsook him. Why? He loved this present world. Can I get a piece of ass? He loved the things he saw, the looseness of the women: Paul, I got to go, I can’t roll with you no more, I got needs. And he let that overcome him.

Who else left Paul? “Crescens to Galatia, Titus unto Dalmatia.” This is the turning away of 2 Timothy 1:15.

This is what happened to Paul’s companions, who were strong in the Lord and the power of his might. Some of you are those guys.

“These are they likewise which are sown on stony ground; who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with gladness”: I’m an Israelite, we got history, I love it. “And have no root in themselves”: they don’t study, they don’t addict themselves to the ministry. I like my sports, I like my porn, and the Bible comes last. “And so endure but for a time”: you only endure this gospel for a time.

“Afterward, when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word’s sake, immediately they are offended.” That is what Paul was warning about: don’t be ashamed of my affliction, suffer it with me, stir up the gift. Affliction is the things that happen to you; persecution is what happens to you for the word’s sake, because you stand strong in this Bible. And Satan will test you: Lord, can I go down and test him? Can I test her?

There was a brother who had a proclivity for men. He was fighting it, about to get married, and went to the gym at two in the morning, when the freaks come out. He heard a noise, looked in the shower, and two men were having sex. Did he walk away? No. He stood there five whole minutes, until they asked him to join in. If you are struggling, stay out of the gym at those hours; do calisthenics at your house. You are trying to fight a spirit; don’t go around spirits like that.

“And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word, And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches”: those that covet riches, that want a piece of the American pie, as we read in 1 Timothy 6:9. “And the lusts of other things entering in”: the cares of this world and riches might not be your thing, but there is something in you nobody else knows. You may hide it very well, but God knows it is there, Satan knows it is there, and you do too. Satan is not going to tempt you with a pork chop. He looks into your soul, sees what you are battling with, and says, Lord, do you mind if I tempt this one? Look, he is going to the gym at two in the morning. They “choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.”

“Alexander the coppersmith did me much evil: the Lord reward him according to his works.” Here is another that was with Paul and turned on him; he disrespected Paul when that great Diana affair was going on.

“Of whom be thou ware also; for he hath greatly withstood our words.” Imagine being in the ministry and then turning against the ministry: that was this man. Paul went through a lot, and we have been through some things too. We have had men in the gospel go online and try to tear this down. Paul went through the same thing.

“At my first answer no man stood with me, but all men forsook me: I pray God that it may not be laid to their charge.”

“And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.” Christ already prophesied it; that is why Paul was not too stressed when all they in Asia turned away from him.

It is hard when you are going through it. 2018 was stressful: brothers were dropping like flies. Brothers and sisters we once called friends, that we broke bread with, that stayed at our homes and knew our families, were offended at the gospel and betrayed the gospel. They hate one another, and nothing good comes out of that. Some of them tried to start Israelite congregations, and they fell overnight. You think God is going to bless your hands after you did so much evil to your brothers and sisters? God isn’t blessing that.

sense.text: “In that day”: the same day, the day of the Lord, we have been reading about. “Shall this song be sung in the land of Judah”: that is talking about Jerusalem. “We have a strong city; salvation will God appoint for walls and bulwarks.”

“Open ye the gates, that the righteous nation which keepeth the truth may enter in.” Not that everybody can enter in. Christians don’t like this, but it is not everybody. Christ said, if you love me, keep my commandments: that is what this is talking about.

The truth is God’s law. So it says, open the gates that the righteous nation which keepeth the law may enter in. That is the only way we get in.

“Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.” This verse is good for those among us who have mental disorders, who take psych meds, whose minds are always in turmoil, who live by Murphy’s Law: whatever can go wrong will go wrong.

Are you at peace? You are worried about getting a wife, getting a husband, a new house, a car, and your mind is not at peace mentally or spiritually. This verse offsets the madness we were smitten with: our minds are troubled and we are on all kinds of medication, but we have to keep our minds stayed on the Lord and trust in the Lord.

“Trust ye in the Lord for ever: for in the Lord Jehovah is everlasting strength.” Jehovah has three syllables: Je-ho-vah. There is no J in Hebrew, so what was there originally? Ya-ha-wah: three syllables. Not Yahweh, which is two. The syllables are showing you: Yahawah, not Jehovah, not Yahweh.

And Christ gives us a secret: the Lord Jehovah of old, the God dealing with us in the Old Testament, was Christ.

“For he bringeth down them that dwell on high”: the Lord Jehovah, Yahawah, which is Christ, brings down them that dwell on high. “The lofty city, he layeth it low; he layeth it low, even to the ground; he bringeth it even to the dust.” Christ is going to lay it low; Christ is going to destroy kingdoms.

precepts.why:
“And had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.”

That is the righteous nation of Isaiah 26:2 for whom the gates are opened: the twelve tribes of Israel. Not everybody.

“Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” God’s law is the truth.

So “the righteous nation which keepeth the truth” is the righteous nation which keeps the law. That is the only way in.

“Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.” The city is New Jerusalem.

The gates of Isaiah 26:2 are opened to those that keep the commandments.

Here is the prophecy: “The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart.” Madness, in your mind.

They say black people don’t like going to doctors. Some of us in here and some of us online have undiagnosed mental disorders. Isaiah 26:3 offsets what we read here: “Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee.” We have to keep our minds on the Lord and trust in him.

Christ gives us a secret here, and they will get mad online. “Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am.”

Christ is letting them know he is the I AM of Exodus: that was me. The Lord Jehovah of Isaiah 26:4 is Christ.

“And God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: and he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.”

That is Christ. Christ is telling you, that’s me. That God you are praying to, the one called Yahweh: that was me back then.

“Lord, shew us the Father, and it sufficeth us.” “Jesus saith unto him, Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip?”

You want to see the Father that created you? I am the Father that created you.

“For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder.” Christ coming is the beginning of government. “And his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father.”

Where does that come from? Christ is saying, all that time, that was me. We know Christ is not the Father, the heavenly Father. But the God that was dealing with us in the Old Testament, Christ says, that was me. That is why he said he came in the volume of the book, and it is written of him.

“All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.” All things were made by Christ, and without Christ nothing was made.

So Christ was letting them know, I am your father, I am the one that created you. Christ is the only begotten of the Father: the Father created Christ alone, and everything else, the Father said, this is your world, you create this. That is how Proverbs 8 speaks of him as daily the Father’s delight, brought up with him. So the Lord Jehovah, the everlasting strength we trust in, is Christ.

sense.text: Christ is going to lay the lofty city even to the dust. “Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered: let them also that hate him flee before him.” The God we are reading about right there is Christ.
“As smoke is driven away, so drive them away: as wax melteth before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.”

“But let the righteous be glad; let them rejoice before God: yea, let them exceedingly rejoice.” That is going to be a hard thing: we are going to rejoice, but we are going to be scared at the same time.
“Extol him that rideth upon the heavens by his name Jah.” People love to say Jah, Jah Rastafari, but it is actually Yah, Y-A-H.

“A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows, is God in his holy habitation. God setteth the solitary in families: he bringeth out those which are bound with chains: but the rebellious dwell in a dry land.” God is going to deliver us, but the rebellious dwell in a dry land.
“The earth shook, the heavens also dropped at the presence of God”: darkness, the skies come down low. “Even Sinai itself was moved at the presence of God, the God of Israel.”

“Thy congregation hath dwelt therein: thou, O God, hast prepared of thy goodness for the poor.” Why does God have to prepare for the poor? Because the wicked would do things to them.

In East Ramapo, Orthodox Jews won enough seats by block voting to control the school board. They voted down the school budgets, eliminated hundreds of teachers and social workers, and spent millions of taxpayer dollars on their own children’s religious private schools, gutting the public schools of some nine thousand black and brown students; one school was shut down and sold to a yeshiva for pennies on the dollar. And they said, if you don’t like it, find yourself another place to live. What you see them doing to the Palestinians in Gaza, you think it isn’t happening over here? It is happening to us over here.

precepts.why: “Let them also that hate him flee before him.” Christ said it in Proverbs: “But he that sinneth against me wrongeth his own soul: all they that hate me love death.”

Let the wicked perish at his presence, let them that hate him flee before him: that is what Habakkuk 3 shows. “O Lord, I have heard thy speech, and was afraid”: I have read the scriptures, and I was afraid. “O Lord, revive thy work”: the work is Israel, being revived. “In wrath remember mercy”: we know the day of the Lord is coming, so in your wrath, Lord, please show mercy.

“God came from Teman”: modern-day Teman is that area of Jordan today. “And the Holy One from mount Paran.” “He had horns coming out of his hand”: horns mean power coming out of his hands. Look at the X-Men and the Avengers with power coming out of their hands: this is where they got it. “And there was the hiding of his power”: he had to hold back the residue of his power.

“Before him went the pestilence, and burning coals went forth at his feet.” That is how fearful it is: every footstep he takes on the earth, there is fire, pestilence, disease and death. “He stood, and measured the earth”: he has to measure his power, how much it takes to take all these nations out, because he could destroy us all like that.

“He beheld, and drove asunder the nations”: that is what we just read in Psalms 68, “let his enemies be scattered.” “And the everlasting mountains were scattered, the perpetual hills did bow: his ways are everlasting.”

We are going to rejoice and be scared at the same time. “And the same hour was there a great earthquake”: destruction. “And the tenth part of the city fell, and in the earthquake were slain of men seven thousand: and the remnant were affrighted.”

Why afraid? Because those alive at that time are going to be saved by the skin of our teeth. The righteous shall scarcely be saved, and that is literal. We usually take it spiritually, that our righteousness is not like God’s, and that is true, but it also means literally, when destruction is all around us. We will be afraid, but we will give glory: the remnant “gave glory to the God of heaven.”

“To them who by patient continuance in well doing seek for glory and honour and immortality, eternal life.” We have to patiently endure in this truth, in well doing, seeking glory, honour, immortality and eternal life.

“But unto them that are contentious”: argumentative, rebellious, “and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, indignation and wrath, Tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that doeth evil”: upon all the wicked Israelites that do evil, “of the Jew first”, the kingdom of Judah, “and also of the Gentile”, the northern kingdom of Israel.

God has prepared of his goodness for the poor. “Evening, and morning, and at noon, will I pray, and cry aloud: and he shall hear my voice.”

We, the poor of the flock, must accustom ourselves to praying evening, morning and noon: three times a day. And he shall hear our voice.

sense.text:
“With my soul have I desired thee in the night”: that is praying at evening time, as in Psalms 55. “Yea, with my spirit within me will I seek thee early”: the morning prayer and the noon prayer.

“For when thy judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world will learn righteousness”: they are going to learn to keep the commandments.

“Let favour be shewed to the wicked, yet will he not learn righteousness.” Who is the wicked? Esau, Edom. Favour is shown to them, and they are in the land, yet they will not learn righteousness. You thought those people follow Torah, follow Tanakh? I don’t care how religious they are: they are against our people. We saw what they did to us with the school system up north, buying the homes, the schools.

“In the land of uprightness will he deal unjustly”: in the land of Israel. Didn’t we just see what he is doing to Gaza, 70 percent of its buildings damaged or destroyed, whole neighbourhoods flattened? Is he not dealing unjustly with the Palestinians? And Israel is working with the UAE and the RSF militias to destroy the black Sudanese, to control Sudan’s ports on the Red Sea, its farmland and its gold.

“And will not behold the majesty of the Lord.” He does not care about God. He doesn’t care about the Bible, about Torah, about Tanakh.

“Lord, when thy hand is lifted up, they will not see”: the prophets are the warning; when our hand is lifted up we are telling them destruction is coming, and they will not see. They won’t acknowledge that God is working in the earth as we prophesy. More people were killed in Sudan in three weeks than in the entire Gaza war, and nobody talks about Sudan: people that look like you and me.

“But they shall see, and be ashamed for their envy at the people.” Regardless, they will see God’s power. They envy us. They may mock the way we look, our noses, our lips, our hair; it is all envy, because we are the children of God.

“Yea, the fire of thine enemies shall devour them.” The them is the group in verse 10: the wicked dealing unjustly in the land of uprightness.
“Lord, thou wilt ordain peace for us: for thou also hast wrought all our works in us.” The peace is going to come with nations rebuked: nations will have to be put down.

“O Lord our God, other lords beside thee have had dominion over us.” Who were these other lords over us? Esau and Ishmael. Esau scattered us: the tribe of Judah to America, the Levites to Saint Domingue, the tribe of Benjamin to the West Indies. King Leopold of Belgium had hands and feet cut off when the rubber quota was not met, while all the European nations stood by. Ishmael did it too: the slave market of Mecca, Zanzibar, brothers castrated and made to watch over harems in Tunisia, and an Ethiopian woman held at auction as a slave in Libya.

“But by thee only will we make mention of thy name.”

“They are dead, they shall not live; they are deceased, they shall not rise: therefore hast thou visited and destroyed them, and made all their memory to perish.” Job elucidates very well on what this verse is saying.

“Thou hast increased the nation, O Lord, thou hast increased the nation”: what nation? The twelve tribes. “Thou art glorified: thou hadst removed it far unto all the ends of the earth.” Israel is going to be everywhere: removed far to the ends of the earth in dominion. We are going to rule the planet.

“Lord, in trouble have they visited thee, they poured out a prayer when thy chastening was upon them.” The only time we cry to the Lord is when we are chastised.

And the chastening is upon us. Young black men found hanging from trees and pillars across the country, and every death ruled a suicide, no foul play. Black people shot by police and by an off-duty ICE agent. A sixteen-year-old boy shot on a porch for trying to return a wallet. This is what we have been reading about in Isaiah 59 and here: no justice. These hangings are not random; it is the same thing as the hangings of the ’40s and ’50s starting all over again, so be careful with your children. We had sixty years of a little liberty that Esau gave us, and we could have done astronomical things, but we dropped the ball; we wanted to sin, we wanted to be like the other nations. Now they are undoing it, and rightfully so, because the Bible has been warning us and we chose to ignore it.

“Like as a woman with child, that draweth near the time of her delivery, is in pain, and crieth out in her pangs; so have we been in thy sight, O Lord.” The things that happen to us, the things we see, are like a woman in travail.

“We have been with child”: the child is Christ, the Messiah. “We have been in pain”: that is captivity. “We have as it were brought forth wind”: we are disobedient; we do not obey God’s commandments.

“We have not wrought any deliverance in the earth”: we have not changed our situation; we have not changed the world the way it is supposed to be. “Neither have the inhabitants of the world fallen”: the inhabitants of the world were supposed to fall when we had power, but they didn’t. We joined with them.

“Thy dead men shall live, together with my dead body shall they arise”: that is talking about what Christ did.

“Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust”: he is telling us to wake up and sing, you that dwell in confusion, in a low state. “For thy dew is as the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast out the dead.” That is deliverance.

“Come, my people, enter thou into thy chambers, and shut thy doors about thee: hide thyself as it were for a little moment, until the indignation be overpast.” There is going to be destruction all around us. That is how much devastation there will be: we are going to be fearful, it will be so much destruction when this day comes.
Why? “For, behold, the Lord cometh out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity: the earth also shall disclose her blood, and shall no more cover her slain.”

precepts.why:
Who is the wicked? “Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places”: Edom returned and built the desolate places; that happened in the Renaissance. They rebuilt their civilization.

“They shall build, but I will throw down”: that is Christ. “And they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” The people, not a person: the Lord has righteous anger against them for ever.

So the wicked of Isaiah 26:10, to whom favour is shown and who will not learn righteousness, is Esau, Edom.

“Be ashamed for their envy at the people”: they envy us. “The heathen shall envy thee”: the heathen means the nations. “But they shall be able to do nothing against thee, saith the Lord.” They can’t do anything against this truth.

What is going to happen in the land of uprightness? “Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth”: if you are humble, as these brothers and sisters are, the meek of the earth. “Which have wrought his judgment”: which have done his laws. “Seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord’s anger.” We want to be hid in the day of the Lord’s anger.

“For Gaza shall be forsaken”: God prophesied that Gaza is going to be forsaken. Put up the map: the names the Bible uses are the same modern names today. “And Ashkelon a desolation”: Ashkelon is right above it. “They shall drive out Ashdod at the noon day”: Ashdod is above Ashkelon, and it tells you the time it is going to happen, at noonday. “And Ekron shall be rooted up.”

That is the fire that shall devour the wicked who deal unjustly in the land of uprightness.

“Lord, thou wilt ordain peace for us”: here is that peace. “And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established in the top of the mountains”: we are going to have the highest government on earth, “exalted above the hills”, above all kingdoms.

“And all nations shall flow unto it. And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob.” It starts with Israel first: the first that come up are all Israel. The other nations will have to be obedient to the commandments, or there will be no rain; they will be subjugated. “For out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.”

“And he shall judge among the nations, and shall rebuke many people”: he is Christ, as we read in Isaiah 26 and in Habakkuk 3. While Jerusalem is established there will still be nations warring, and they will be subdued. Then “nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.” That is peace.

Israel is going to come back to the land in increments; all Israel will not be there at the same time initially. “And I will set a sign among them, and I will send those that escape of them unto the nations”: those that escape the destruction are the 144. The Lord is going to dispatch the 144 to the nations: “to Tarshish”, Spain, “Pul”, Libya, “and Lud”, Lydia, “to Tubal”, Turkey, “and Javan”, Greece, “to the isles afar off.”

“That have not heard my fame, neither have seen my glory; and they shall declare my glory among the Gentiles.” There is a remnant out there that has not heard God’s fame, and the 144 shall declare his glory among the Gentiles.

“And they shall bring all your brethren for an offering unto the Lord out of all nations upon horses, and in chariots, and in litters, and upon mules, and upon swift beasts, to my holy mountain Jerusalem.” There are more Israelites out there: go get them. Isaiah 2 is in effect, but all Israel is not there yet. “And I will also take of them for priests and for Levites, saith the Lord.”

A lot of times we read about the deliverance and say everybody is there. Everybody is not there yet: Israel numbers as the sand of the sea, and the Lord will dispatch the 144 to gather their brethren.

Job elucidates very well what Isaiah 26:14 is saying. “Yet he shall perish for ever like his own dung”: like his own shit; that is what the Bible says. “They which have seen him shall say, Where is he?”

“He shall fly away as a dream, and shall not be found: yea, he shall be chased away as a vision of the night.” A vision of the night is a nightmare: God is letting us know he is going to take away the wicked, and they will be like a bad dream to us. “The eye also which saw him shall see him no more; neither shall his place any more behold him.”

“His children shall seek to please the poor, and his hands shall restore their goods.” Everything Esau took from us, Ishmael too, they are going to be forced to give back.

“Thou hast increased the nation”: here is the precept. “Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified.”

“A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation”: that is what Isaiah meant by “thou hast increased the nation.” “I the Lord will hasten it in his time”: God is going to speed this thing up.

What does “removed it far unto all the ends of the earth” mean? Not just the land will be ours; the earth will be ours.

“And the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven”: the whole planet earth, “shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High, whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him.” Everybody shall obey Christ.

“All this have I spoken before thee, O Lord, because thou madest the world for our sakes.” The world was made for Israel’s sake, and Israel is going to be removed far to the ends of the earth in dominion.

“They poured out a prayer when thy chastening was upon them.” “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.”

We are going to seek God, but we only seek God when we are afflicted.

“Therefore is judgment far from us, neither doth justice overtake us: we wait for light, but behold obscurity”: confusion. “For brightness, but we walk in darkness. We grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as if we had no eyes.” Black people and Latin people act as if we have no eyes. We see the evil, and then we say, some of them are good, they ain’t all like that.

“We are in desolate places as dead men”: we are like the walking dead. “We roar all like bears, and mourn sore like doves”: that is us crying and screaming in the streets. “We look for judgment, but there is none; for salvation, but it is far off from us. For our transgressions are multiplied before thee, and our sins testify against us.”

“And judgment is turned away backward”: the judgment we seek in this wicked kingdom is always turned away backward. “And justice standeth afar off”: we look for justice, but it stands far off from us. “For truth is fallen in the street, and equity cannot enter. Yea, truth faileth; and he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey.”

That is what we are watching on the screen: Mario Kaiser Jr. in Charlotte, Earl Smith in Albany, an unidentified man in Oakland, Trey Reed at Delta State University with the back of his head smashed in, Javon Givens in Albuquerque, Torrence Medley in Brookfield, Kyle Basinger in Marietta, all found hanging and all ruled suicide. Keith Porter shot by an off-duty ICE agent; Dr. Linda Davis killed by a driver fleeing ICE; Dequaine Johnson shot by police in Grand Rapids. Sixteen-year-old Jordan Mitchell in Houston found a wallet, went to return it, held it up to the doorbell camera, and the homeowner shot him for trespassing, was released without charges, and the boy’s family was ordered to pay the legal fees. No justice, no peace.

This is the verse that explains a woman in travail. “As when a woman with child in the ninth month bringeth forth her son, with two or three hours of her birth great pains compass her womb, which pains, when the child cometh forth, they slack not a moment: Even so shall not the plagues be slack to come upon the earth.”

Those two or three hours can be two or three years or two or three months, depending on how quickly the prophecies come to pass. The plagues come on the earth like those pains, one after another.

“In all their affliction he was afflicted”: in all our affliction, God was afflicted. “And the angel of his presence saved them: in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; and he bare them, and carried them all the days of old.”

“We have been with child”: “But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons.”

Christ coming was to redeem those of us who were under the law: the twelve tribes. The child Israel has been with is Christ, the Messiah.

“Together with my dead body shall they arise”: “Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. Then said the Jews, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days? But he spake of the temple of his body.”

The dead body of Isaiah 26:19 is Christ’s body, raised up the third day.

“Jesus, when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost”: Christ died. “And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake”: there was an earthquake, “and the rocks rent”: the rocks were split in two.

“And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose, And came out of the graves after his resurrection, and went into the holy city, and appeared unto many.” Imagine how scary that must have been: I buried you two years ago, and here you are knocking at my door.

Christ is letting you know: when he was resurrected, the dead all around came back to life. “Thy dead men shall live, together with my dead body shall they arise.”

“And the earth shall cast out the dead”: “For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first.” The dead in Christ are those brothers and sisters that believed; they shall rise first.

“Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds.”
“Come, my people, enter thou into thy chambers”: “Who are these that fly as a cloud, and as the doves to their windows?” Who are these that fly as a cloud: in the chariot. Chambers and windows.

Chambers and windows: “And they heard a great voice from heaven saying unto them, Come up hither. And they ascended up to heaven in a cloud; and their enemies beheld them.”

Those are they that fly as a cloud, entering their chambers and hiding for a little moment until the indignation be overpast.

“The earth also shall disclose her blood, and shall no more cover her slain.” “As Babylon hath caused the slain of Israel to fall, so at Babylon shall fall the slain of all the earth.” All the slain of the earth will be judged on Babylon.

“And in her was found the blood of prophets, and of saints, and of all that were slain upon the earth.”

In Babylon is found the blood of all that were slain upon the earth. The judgment that is going to come to this country, this kingdom, is going to be the worst of all.

sense.text: Remember what we read in Isaiah 26: the Lord comes out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity. “And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it”: this is Christ. “From whose face the earth and the heaven fled away”: he is in full power. “And there was found no place for them”: nobody opens their damn mouth against Christ.

“And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God”: this is everybody. “And the books were opened”: the Bibles were opened. “And another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.”

“And the sea gave up the dead which were in it”: this is what we read in the last verse of Isaiah 26. “And death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them”: hell is the grave; those that died and were in the graves were given up.

“And they were judged every man according to their works”: whether we were in God’s laws or against God’s laws. That is the judgment.

“And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death.” Death is finished at that point. And it is not just death and hell: the nations go with it, because they are judged according to their works.

“And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.” Let’s see who is in the book of life: whether the Chinese, or the white man, or the Arabs are written there. Who is written in the book? Israel, Daniel’s people, not everybody. So whosoever was not found written in the book of life includes all the nations.

precepts.why:
“For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son.” The heavenly Father judges no man. Christ is the one judging everything.

So him that sits on the great white throne, from whose face the earth and the heaven flee away, is Christ.
We are going to be judged according to our works: “For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.”

“For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ.” A lot of times we thought it was the Father judging us; it is actually Christ. “That every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.”

Who is written in the book of life? “And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.”

Those written in the book are Israel, Daniel’s people. Not everybody.

They hate this one. “Fear thou not, O Jacob my servant, saith the Lord: for I am with thee; for I will make a full end of all the nations whither I have driven thee: but I will not make a full end of thee”: I will not destroy you, “but correct thee in measure.” God is correcting us in measure; “yet will I not leave thee wholly unpunished.”

The nations are made a full end of; Israel, written in the book, is not.

“Let the multitude perish then, which was born in vain”: all the nations, the Bible says, were born in vain. “And let my grape be kept, and my plant”: let the Israelites be kept. “For with great labour have I made it perfect.”

So whosoever was not found written in the book of life, cast into the lake of fire, is all the nations.
